concept.name: Warehouse receipt
concept.definition: A document certifying possession of a commodity in a licensed or exchange-approved warehouse, recognized for delivery purposes in settlement of futures contracts.
concept.intuition: The warehouse receipt is the paper (or electronic) title to goods sitting in an approved silo or vault — delivering the receipt is delivering the commodity.
concept.mechanics: Commodities must be stored in exchange-approved facilities and meet deliverable grades; the receipt evidences that stock and circulates through the clearing organization during delivery, transferring ownership from short to long. It functions as a negotiable delivery instrument alongside alternatives such as shipping certificates.
concept.failure_modes: The system rests on warehouse integrity: fraud, double-pledged receipts, or metal/grain that fails inspection breaks the deliverable supply and can trigger market disruption, as in historical warehouse-receipt scandals.
concept.misconceptions: A warehouse receipt is not the same as a delivery notice — the notice declares intent to deliver, while the receipt is the title document that actually conveys the commodity.
concept.example: In a copper futures delivery, the short's clearing member passes a registered LME/CME warehouse receipt for 25 metric tons in an approved warehouse to the assigned long in exchange for the invoice payment.

citations.source: CFTC Glossary: A Guide to the Language of the Futures Industry
